name: Shakti remote-viewing design (untested): modulated 40 Hz occipital
origin: Todd Murphy (Shakti software; extrapolation from Persinger-lab papers)
summary: Murphy's proposed Shakti design for remote viewing: the modulated 40 Hz signal over both occipital lobes, just above the bony ridge at the back of the head, for 20 min. He links it to the occipital 7 Hz activity Persinger's lab reported in the remote viewer Ingo Swann, and writes that the procedures on his page have not been tested.
setting: Practise remote-viewing exercises (Murphy). For a fair test, judge results blind, e.g. with the app's Photo-target trial guide.
schedule: The vendor's general Shakti rules: at most every 72 h or once a week, never on consecutive days; a series of 3 or 6 sessions, then a 21-day break.
notes: Four coils over the occipital lobes, above the bony ridge (O1, PO3, O2, PO4), all with the same signal; the sites are an inference from 'application of the modulated 40hz signal over the occipital lobes'. The other four channels stay unused. The Shakti's modulated 40 Hz file is proprietary; it is approximated by the built-in phase-modulated sine (a 40 Hz carrier drifting between about 38.5 and 41.5 Hz every 2 s, 1-ms points). The vendor calibrates its modulated 40 Hz signal at 10 mG (1 µT), the default here. Murphy also names the right occipito-temporo-parietal region and the right frontal, right occipital and right temporal lobes as candidate sites. The two-phase psychic design (frontal, then occipital) is murphy-shakti-psi-rv-untested. Persinger's lab reported that Swann's accuracy tracked occipital 7 Hz activity during a 30-min circumcerebral exposure (Persinger et al. 2002, one subject, one lab); it has not been independently replicated. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). The vendor notes that occipital stimulation could in principle blur vision: stop if your sight changes. Do not use results for decisions about real people, places or money. Not for people with epilepsy; stop on distress.
source: Murphy, Shakti demo: Remote viewing https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/remote_v.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Psychic skills https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/psychic.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Modulated 40 Hz (obe45) signal (10 mG calibration) https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/obe45_consent.htm ; Persinger et al. 2002, Percept Mot Skills 94:927 (remote viewing with Ingo Swann) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12081299/ ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Safety - how often https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/how_often_is_safe.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Taking breaks https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/break.htm ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 (8 Coil Shakti amygdala signal, sham-controlled) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
